transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. Smith. Thanks for coming in today—what brings you in to see me?

Hi Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Thanks for seeing me. 

Um... I guess I'm mostly just dealing with some work stress. I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, I know you probably see people with much bigger problems. Is it okay if I just explain a little bit about what's been going on? 

I'm a transportation inspector, and... well, things got a little complicated after I won this county safety award recently. I mean, I was really grateful for it, but ever since then, it just seems like certain people at work are... I really don't want to sound like a complainer, but they've been twisting my inspection reports. And they keep asking these really pointed budget questions, almost like they're trying to make me look crooked. 

My supervisor says it's just a normal review process, and I always try to be a good team player and listen to him, but... I can just tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. I hope that doesn't sound terrible to say out loud. Does that make sense?
How long has this feeling that people at work are coordinating against you been going on—days, weeks, or longer?

Um... well, I guess it's been a little longer than just a few weeks. I really hope I don't sound, you know, paranoid or anything for saying this... but it's actually been going on for about a year now. 

Pretty much right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative I mentioned. I really tried to just brush it off at first, because I always want to get along with everyone and be easy to work with, you know? I didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing. But... yeah, about a year. Is it okay that I let it go on this long before talking to someone about it?

Before this happened at work, would you say you've generally been a suspicious or distrustful person in other areas of your life—like with friends, family, or in past jobs—or is this kind of concern about people plotting against you something totally new for you?

No, no, definitely not. I've always tried to be the kind of person who gets along with everybody. I mean, I love my family, and I've always had a good relationship with my friends. I really pride myself on being easygoing and trusting, you know? 

I've never had any issues like this at my old jobs, either. I always got good performance reviews and got along great with my coworkers. That's why this whole thing at my current job is just so... confusing for me. I really don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who goes around looking for trouble or suspecting the worst in people. I'm really not. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, during this past year?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I've never experienced anything like that. I really hope I haven't given you the impression that I'm, you know, totally losing touch with reality or anything. 

I'm just a normal guy dealing with a really stressful work situation. I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine, I promise. I just... I just know what's happening with my reports and the way they're treating me. That's all it is. Is it okay that I just have this one specific issue going on? I really want to be helpful and give you the right answers.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief (coworkers coordinating to discredit him via altered reports and pointed questioning) persisting for about one year. There is no history of premorbid suspiciousness/paranoid traits, no hallucinations, no disorganized speech/behavior, and no negative symptoms, arguing against schizophrenia. Functioning appears preserved outside the delusional theme, and there is no evidence of a mood episode preceding or accompanying the delusion, ruling out a psychotic mood disorder. The encapsulated, plausible-sounding persecutory delusion with preserved insight into other areas of life and no prior paranoid personality pattern is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
